cards.subject: Patch Docker: docker cp can bypass read-only mounts
cards.preheader: Docker Engine v29.10.1 also fixes failing builds and concurrent network rm errors.
cards.hook: A process running during `docker cp` can modify host directories behind your read-only bind mounts. The fix was released on 24 Nov.
cards.tip: Upgrade to Docker Engine `v29.10.1` to close `CVE-2026-135124` and `CVE-2026-135844` and fix build and `docker network rm` failures.
steps: Upgrade Docker Engine to `v29.10.1` on every host
Run `docker login` to see the new OATs authentication options
Rebuild an image and confirm build context uploads with `Expect: 100-continue` succeed
cards.why: Your host directories stay protected during `docker cp`, and your builds and network removals stop failing.
number: Docker Engine release with the fix
cards.deadline: Upgrade now: `CVE-2026-135124` and `CVE-2026-135844` allow host directory overwrites during `docker cp` and unbounded file reads.

riddle.q: I am a number, yet I am not a number, and I am not even equal to myself. What am I?
riddle.why: NaN == NaN is False, so use math.isnan() or pandas isna() to find missing values.

cards.subject: One setting keeps Copilot reviews off your org's bill
cards.preheader: From 30 Dec, unset Copilot code review billing switches to Organization.
cards.hook: From 30 Dec, GitHub switches unset Copilot code review billing to `Organization`. That can increase your organization's spending.
cards.tip: Set Copilot code review billing to `Member` so licensed members keep using their own Copilot entitlement.
steps: Open your enterprise or organization Copilot policy settings
Change Copilot code review billing from `Default (Member)` to `Member`
Ask an enterprise owner if your enterprise manages this setting
cards.why: Code reviews by licensed members stay on their own entitlement, not your organization's bill.
cards.deadline: Select `Member` before 30 Dec. If you already chose `Member` or `Organization`, your choice stays in effect.

riddle.q: I remember every change you ever made and can take you back to any moment, but I am happiest when you commit. What am I?
riddle.why: Every commit is a save point you can return to with git checkout or git revert.
